evidence: fn-bpnp-rotation-quiescentp (books/bp-node-progress.lisp:1507) requires (null (fn-bpn-machine-state-jobs base)) and (equal (fn-bpn-machine-state-next-token base) 0); the kind-19 checkpoint (fn-bpnr-checkpoint: generation, held, handoffs, frontier, next-arrival, covered) carries no jobs, so fn-bpnp-rotate-step answers (:rotation-refused G) for any journal with a queued/requeued receipt or report job. Image c4-gate@7a6499ec3, test_disconnected_delivery_restarts_and_releases_only_matching_obligation: after one dispatch pass leaves two requeued receipt jobs, bp-node checkpoint prints 'BP queue recovered jobs=2', 'BP journal rotation generation=1', 'BP journal rotation refused generation=1' and never reaches the stage cut. A journal truncated to its first record (one job) is refused the same way; test_rotation_killed_at_each_cut_keeps_held_rows (no jobs) rotates.
fix: Statement-first in ACL2: either the checkpoint carries the base jobs (a codec field, fn-bpnr-checkpoint-of-statep over them, replay equal to full recovery with the jobs, teeth: a rotation that drops an owed job is refuted) and quiescence drops the jobs/next-token clauses, or the spec states that rotation waits for the queue to drain and the host drains it before rotating. Then restore the stage-cut observation in test_disconnected_delivery_restarts_and_releases_only_matching_obligation.
notes: 10-07 C5 decision (statement first, before any proof): option A, the checkpoint carries the base machine's owed work. Option B (rotation waits for the queue to drain) is refused: an owed receipt to a disconnected peer may never drain, so B leaves the generation to grow to its 8192-record bound with no rotation, a liveness hole the spec would have to state as one. Statements the proof lane enters before proving: (S1) fn-bpnr-checkpoint gains the base machine's JOBS and NEXT-TOKEN (codec field; fn-bpnr-checkpoint-octets round-trips them; the depth budget fn-bpnr-depth-budget already scales with max-jobs); (S2) fn-bpnr-checkpoint-of-statep requires them equal to (fn-bpn-machine-state-jobs (fn-bpnf-base st)) and -next-token, and fn-bpnp-rotation-quiescentp drops its two clauses (null jobs, next-token 0) and nothing else; (S3) fn-bpnr-replay-from seeds the replay's base with the checkpoint's jobs and next-token, and fn-bpnr-recover-from-checkpoint-equals-full-recover and fn-bpnr-rotation-crash-recovers-old-or-new keep their statements, now over states that owe jobs; (S4, new keystone) recovery from a rotation checkpoint of a state that owes jobs yields a base machine whose jobs and next-token equal the state's at rotation; teeth: a checkpoint whose jobs are NIL for a state that owes one fails fn-bpnr-checkpoint-of-statep (a witness with one queued receipt job), so a rotation that drops an owed job is refuted. Then restore the stage-cut observation in tests.test_bp_node_native test_disconnected_delivery_restarts_and_releases_only_matching_obligation and run it on an image.
reviewer: mechanism established by tracing fn-bpnp-rotate-step and by truncating a dumped journal (hbox:/tank/fn/scratch/bp-residual/jdump, jx*): every variant with a job is refused.
scenario: A node that ever queued a receipt or report job and still owes it cannot rotate: natural rotation (fn-bpnrd-due-rotation-event) answers NIL on quiescence, so the generation fills toward its 8192-record bound while jobs are owed. The documented stage-cut recovery claim (owed receipt jobs survive a death before selection) cannot be exercised.
title: bp-node checkpoint and natural rotation refuse whenever the base machine has any job, so owed receipt jobs make the journal unrotatable and the stage-cut recovery case unreachable
